column1: # Per-file survivor ratchet for tool/mutation.sh (#280).
# <lib/ source path><TAB><maximum surviving mutants>
# A SURVIVOR is a mutant the file's test scope did not notice (the tool's
# "Undetected" count, which includes mutants no test covers at all). The numbers
# are seeded from the 2026-09-02/03 pilot, so the ratchet can only ever go DOWN:
# kill a survivor, lower the number in the same commit. Raising one means the
# suite stopped noticing something it used to catch — that is a regression in
# the tests, and it is closed with an assertion, never with a bigger cap.
# Some survivors are EQUIVALENT mutants (the mutated program cannot behave
# differently — see TESTING.md), which is why a file's floor is rarely 0. An
# equivalent mutant is documented in the closing issue, not asserted away with a
# test that contradicts the contract.
# Files absent from this list are reported but not ratcheted.
# Measured with this tool (mutation.sh, same-name test + importers):
#   dates.dart         39 mutants, 3 survivors, 5m45
#   effective_due.dart 37 mutants, 5 survivors, 1m06 — all five are the
#     equivalent mutants #277 characterised (two Object.hash argument
#     permutations, `<=`->`<` on operands that are equal, `>= 10`->`> 10`
#     around substring(0, 10), and deleting a `seen.remove` the memo makes
#     unobservable). The pilot's 4 predates #277's own change to that file and
#     no run reproduces it, so the cap is the number the committed tool
#     actually produces.
#   store.dart      56 mutants, 0 survivors, 9m21 (#279 batch 3)
#   task_view.dart  86 mutants, 0 survivors, 6m36 (#279 batch 3)
#   quick_add_parse.dart 11 mutants, 1 survivor, 0m30 — `(?:on\s+)?` -> `(?:on\s-)?`
#     in the trailing-date pattern. Equivalent: the phrase is never removed
#     from the title (the parser only reports the date), so the match extent is
#     observable solely through the strip-leaves-title rule, and the required
#     leading `\s+` cannot match at index 0 of a trimmed title — the strip can
#     never come out empty either way. Checked by brute force over 1080 inputs
#   reconcile.dart  285 mutants, 8 survivors, 1h03 (#279 batch 3) — every
#     mutant that RAN and returned was killed. Seven are the `Object.hash`
#     argument permutations on the decision classes' `hashCode` getters, on
#     lines no test in test/sync executes (equal values still hash equal, so
#     covering them cannot kill them). The eighth is a TIMEOUT:
#     `orderParentsFirst`'s `var progressed = false` flipped to `true` never
#     leaves its `while (true)`, so the run is killed at the per-mutant
#     timeout and the report has no text to quote for it. The pilot's 1
#     counted neither class; no run of the committed tool reproduces it.
# The other four are the pilot's counts, taken BEFORE #277/#278 landed: they
# are upper bounds, and the first run of each should come in under them.
